zmanim.noDegreeTimeNote: This calculation is based on the sun reaching a set angle below the horizon, which never happens here on a short summer night — so fixed-minute opinions are used instead.

descriptions.alos90: Dawn as a fixed 90 minutes before sunrise — the time to walk 4 mil at 22½ minutes each; earlier (more stringent) than the 72-minute dawn.
descriptions.alos198: Dawn with the sun 19.8° below the horizon — the degree equivalent of a 90-minute dawn, so it tracks the same twilight at any latitude or season.
descriptions.alos18: Dawn with the sun 18° below the horizon — the start of astronomical twilight, when the sky first begins to lighten.
descriptions.alosBaalHatanya: Dawn per the Baal HaTanya — the sun 16.9° below the horizon; the dawn on which his day and seasonal hours are based.
descriptions.alos72Zmanis: Dawn as 72 seasonal (proportional) minutes before sunrise — one-tenth of the day, so it stretches and shrinks with the season rather than staying a fixed 72 clock-minutes.
descriptions.alosHashachar: Dawn with the sun 16.1° below the horizon — the mainstream degree-based alot, the equivalent of a 72-minute dawn, tracking the same twilight at any latitude or season.
descriptions.alos72: Dawn as a fixed 72 minutes before sunrise — the time to walk 4 mil at 18 minutes each (Rambam and Rishonim). This is the dawn the Magen Avraham uses to measure his seasonal-hour day.
descriptions.alos60: Dawn as a fixed 60 minutes before sunrise — a lenient dawn followed in some communities.
descriptions.misheyakir115: An early, stringent misheyakir — the sun 11.5° below the horizon (≈50 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual gap varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir11: The sun 11° below the horizon (≈48 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual gap varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir102: The most common misheyakir — the sun 10.2° below the horizon (≈44 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; the actual gap varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir95: A later, more lenient misheyakir — the sun 9.5° below the horizon (≈41 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; varies by place and season).
descriptions.misheyakir765: The latest of the common misheyakir opinions — the sun 7.65° below the horizon (≈32 min before sunrise in Jerusalem near the equinox; varies by place and season).
descriptions.sunrise: Sunrise (hanetz) — the sun's upper edge clears the sea-level horizon and the Vilna Gaon's halachic day begins. The vatikin finish the morning Shema just before it and begin the Amidah exactly at sunrise.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaMGA90: End of the 3rd seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with a 90-minute day — measured from a dawn 90 min before sunrise to nightfall 90 min after sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaMGA18: End of the 3rd seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with an 18° day — measured from an 18° dawn to an 18° nightfall.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaMGA161: End of the 3rd seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with a 16.1° day — the degree form of his 72-minute day, dawn to nightfall at 16.1°.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaMGA: End of the 3rd seasonal hour by the Magen Avraham — the day measured from dawn (72 min before sunrise) to nightfall (72 min after sunset), an earlier deadline than the Vilna Gaon.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaBaalHatanya: End of the 3rd seasonal hour per the Baal HaTanya — the day measured between his own (slightly depressed) sunrise and sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanShmaGRA: End of the 3rd seasonal hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — the day measured from sunrise to sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaMGA90: End of the 4th seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with a 90-minute day (dawn 90 min before sunrise to nightfall 90 min after sunset).
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaMGA18: End of the 4th seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with an 18° day.
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaMGA161: End of the 4th seasonal hour, Magen Avraham with a 16.1° day — the degree form of his 72-minute day.
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaMGA: End of the 4th seasonal hour by the Magen Avraham — the day measured from dawn (72 min) to nightfall (72 min).
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaBaalHatanya: End of the 4th seasonal hour per the Baal HaTanya — measured between his own sunrise and sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanTfilaGRA: End of the 4th seasonal hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — the day measured from sunrise to sunset.
descriptions.sofZmanAchilasChametzMGA: Latest time to eat chametz — the end of the 4th seasonal hour by the Magen Avraham (day from dawn, 72 min before sunrise, to nightfall, 72 min after sunset).
descriptions.sofZmanAchilasChametzGRA: Latest time to eat chametz — the end of the 4th seasonal hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA; day from sunrise to sunset).
descriptions.sofZmanBiurChametzMGA: Latest time to burn the chametz — the end of the 5th seasonal hour by the Magen Avraham (day from dawn, 72 min, to nightfall, 72 min).
descriptions.sofZmanBiurChametzGRA: Latest time to burn the chametz — the end of the 5th seasonal hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA; day from sunrise to sunset).
descriptions.chatzos: Solar midday (chatzot) — the sun at its highest, exactly halfway between sunrise and sunset. Midday for both the Vilna Gaon and the Magen Avraham.
descriptions.minchaGedola30: Earliest Mincha as a fixed 30 minutes after midday — a common practice, since half a seasonal hour is close to 30 clock-minutes near the equinox.
descriptions.minchaGedola: Earliest time to pray Mincha — half a seasonal hour after midday (6½ seasonal hours into the Vilna Gaon's sunrise-to-sunset day).
descriptions.minchaGedolaBaalHatanya: Earliest Mincha per the Baal HaTanya — half a seasonal hour after his midday.
descriptions.minchaGedola161: Earliest Mincha on a Magen Avraham 16.1° day — 6½ seasonal hours measured from a 16.1° dawn to a 16.1° nightfall.
descriptions.minchaKetana: Preferred time to pray Mincha — 9½ seasonal hours into the Vilna Gaon's sunrise-to-sunset day (2½ hours before sunset).
descriptions.minchaKetanaBaalHatanya: Preferred Mincha per the Baal HaTanya — 9½ seasonal hours into his day.
descriptions.minchaKetana161: Preferred Mincha on a Magen Avraham 16.1° day — 9½ seasonal hours from a 16.1° dawn to a 16.1° nightfall.
descriptions.plagHamincha: 10¾ seasonal hours into the Vilna Gaon's sunrise-to-sunset day (1¼ hours before sunset) — the earliest one may pray Maariv or accept Shabbat.
descriptions.plagBaalHatanya: Plag ha-Mincha per the Baal HaTanya — 10¾ seasonal hours into his day, 1¼ hours before his sunset.
descriptions.candleLighting: Candle lighting before Shabbat / Yom Tov — the set number of minutes before sunset (18 by default; 40 is the Jerusalem custom).
descriptions.sunset: Sunset (shkiah) — the sun's upper edge dips below the sea-level horizon. Shabbat and Yom Tov begin and the doubtful twilight (bein ha-shmashot) starts; the end of the Vilna Gaon's halachic day.
descriptions.tzaisGeonim: Nightfall per the Baal HaTanya (Siddur of the Alter Rebbe) — the sun 5.95° below the horizon (≈24 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox), an early Geonim-type depression angle; earlier than the mainstream 8.5° three-small-stars.
descriptions.tzaisGeonim645: R' Tukachinsky's end of a minor rabbinic fast — three medium stars, the sun 6.45° below the horizon (≈26 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox); one of the Geonim depression angles.
descriptions.tzaisGeonim7083: R' Moshe Feinstein's end of a minor fast (for one to whom fasting is hard) — three medium stars, the sun 7.083° below the horizon (≈29 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox); a Geonim depression angle.
descriptions.tzais: Nightfall when three small stars are visible — the sun 8.5° below the horizon (≈36 min after sunset in Jerusalem near the equinox), per Rabbi Meir Posen (Ohr Meir); the mainstream nightfall, when the new halachic day begins.
descriptions.tzaisAteretTorah: Nightfall per Yeshivat Ateret Torah (Chacham Yosef Harari-Raful) — a fixed 40 minutes after sunset, common in many Sephardic communities.
descriptions.tzais42: A fixed 42 minutes after sunset — a practical nightfall some communities use to end Shabbat and Yom Tov.
descriptions.tzais50: A fixed 50 minutes after sunset — Rav Moshe Feinstein's nightfall (Igros Moshe) for the New York area, relied on to end Shabbat and Yom Tov.
descriptions.tzais60: A fixed 60 minutes after sunset — a stringent practical nightfall followed in some communities.
descriptions.tzais72: Rabbeinu Tam's stringent nightfall — a fixed 72 minutes after sunset (4 mil × 18 min). Relied on to end Shabbat, Yom Tov and Yom Kippur.
descriptions.tzais161: Rabbeinu Tam's nightfall as a depression angle — the sun 16.1° below the horizon, the degree form of his 72-minute nightfall, so it tracks twilight at any latitude.
descriptions.tzais72Zmanis: Rabbeinu Tam's 72-minute nightfall reckoned in seasonal (proportional) minutes — one-tenth of the day after sunset, so it varies with the season.
descriptions.tzais18: Nightfall with the sun 18° below the horizon — the end of astronomical twilight, when full darkness sets in.
descriptions.tzais90: A fixed 90 minutes after sunset — a very stringent nightfall (4 mil at 22½ min each) some follow for Rabbeinu Tam.
descriptions.chatzosLaila: Solar midnight (chatzot ha-laila) — the halachic midpoint of the night, exactly halfway between sunset and sunrise.
descriptions.shaahZmanisMGA: The length of one seasonal hour by the Magen Avraham — the day measured from dawn (72 min before sunrise) to nightfall (72 min after sunset), so the hour runs longer.
descriptions.shaahZmanisGRA: The length of one seasonal hour by the Vilna Gaon (GRA) — the day measured from sunrise to sunset.

baseDescriptions.alos: Dawn (alot ha-shachar) — the first light of morning and the start of the halachic day for many mitzvot. The degree-based opinions track the same twilight at any latitude; the fixed- and proportional-minute ones do not.
baseDescriptions.misheyakir: Earliest time to don tallit and tefillin — when there is enough light to recognize a casual acquaintance, or to tell the tzitzit's blue thread from the white.
baseDescriptions.sofZmanShma: Latest time to recite the morning Shema — the end of the third seasonal hour. The Vilna Gaon measures the day sunrise→sunset; the Magen Avraham measures it dawn→nightfall, giving an earlier deadline.
baseDescriptions.sofZmanTfila: Latest time for the morning Amidah (Shacharit) — the end of the fourth seasonal hour, by the same day-length opinions as the Shema deadline.
baseDescriptions.achilasChametz: Erev Pesach: the latest time to eat chametz — the end of the fourth seasonal hour.
baseDescriptions.biurChametz: Erev Pesach: the latest time to burn / dispose of the chametz — the end of the fifth seasonal hour.
baseDescriptions.minchaGedola: Earliest time to pray Mincha — half a seasonal hour after midday (6½ seasonal hours into the day).
baseDescriptions.minchaKetana: Preferred time to pray Mincha — 9½ seasonal hours into the day, 2½ hours before its end.
baseDescriptions.plagHamincha: 10¾ seasonal hours into the day — 1¼ seasonal hours before its end; the earliest one may pray Maariv or accept Shabbat.
baseDescriptions.tzais: Nightfall (tzeit ha-kochavim) — the stars come out and the new halachic day begins. Opinions run from an early few-stars nightfall to Rabbeinu Tam's stringent 72-minute one used to end Shabbat and Yom Tov.
baseDescriptions.shaahZmanis: The length of one seasonal (halachic) hour — a twelfth of the halachic day; zmanim like Sof zman Shema are counted in these hours. Shown as a duration (h:mm:ss), not a clock time.

familyDescriptions.degrees: The sun reaches a set angle below the horizon. The same angle everywhere — but at high latitudes in summer the sun may never get that low, and then the opinion simply has no time that day.
familyDescriptions.fixedMinutes: A fixed count of clock minutes before sunrise or after sunset. Always defined wherever the sun rises and sets, but it takes no account of twilight lasting longer in summer.
familyDescriptions.seasonalMinutes: A count of seasonal (zmaniyos) minutes, where one minute is a sixtieth of a halachic hour — and one halachic hour is a twelfth of the daylight. So the “minute” stretches in summer and shrinks in winter.
familyDescriptions.dawnToNightfall: The halachic hours are twelfths of a day measured from dawn to nightfall — the longer day of the Magen Avraham. Its hours begin earlier and run longer, so this time falls earlier.
familyDescriptions.sunriseToSunset: The halachic hours are twelfths of a day measured from sunrise to sunset — the day of the Vilna Gaon, and, from his own true sunrise, the Baal HaTanya.
familyDescriptions.solar: The position of the sun itself.

panel.zmanimSettingsHint: More zmanim and opinions can be shown via the calendar settings.
panel.lehumraNote: Times are rounded to the stringent whole minute (lehumra).
panel.lehumraDetail:
Every displayed time is rounded to a whole minute in the stricter direction — by less than a minute, and only in the display; the underlying calculation stays exact.
Rounded DOWN (deadlines — no later than): sof zman Shema and Tefila, the chametz deadlines, shkia, candle lighting before Shabbat and Yom Tov, and the start of a fast.
Rounded UP (onsets — no earlier than): alot ha-shachar, misheyakir, hanetz, chatzot, mincha gedola and ketana, plag ha-mincha, tzeit ha-kochavim, havdala, the end of a fast, and candle lighting after nightfall (2nd Yom Tov night, Motzei Shabbat).
panel.observedPostponed: Observed later this year because of Shabbat.
panel.observedAdvanced: Observed earlier this year because of Shabbat.

learning.title: Daily learning
learning.dafYomiInfo: One page (daf) of the Babylonian Talmud a day; the worldwide cycle completes the entire Talmud in about 7½ years.
learning.yerushalmiYomiInfo: One page of the Jerusalem Talmud a day (Vilna edition); the cycle takes about 4¼ years. No page is learned on Yom Kippur or Tisha BeAv.
learning.mishnaYomitInfo: Two mishnayot a day, completing the entire Mishnah in about six years.
learning.nachYomiInfo: One chapter of Nevi'im (Prophets) or Ketuvim (Writings) a day, completing Nach in 742 days.
learning.tehillimInfo: Tehillim (Psalms) divided across the days of the Hebrew month — the whole book is finished every month.
learning.rambamInfo: One chapter of the Rambam's Mishneh Torah a day; the cycle completes all 14 books in just under three years.
learning.pirkeiAvotInfo: A chapter of Pirkei Avot is studied on Shabbat afternoons between Pesach and Rosh Hashanah.

settings.candleOffsetHint: Minutes before sunset (40 is common in Jerusalem).
settings.elevationHint: Adjusts sunrise, sunset and the zmanim measured from them for the location's height above sea level. Standard published times use sea level — enable this only if your community follows visible-horizon times. Degree-based zmanim, chatzot and candle lighting are unaffected. For the best result, use your device location rather than a city search — the elevation is then detected for your exact spot, not the city center.
